home.description: Your browser’s native router made powerful. Routes, guards, data and views on the Navigation API.
home.hero.title: Your browser’s native router made powerful
home.hero.lede: Extends the browser’s built-in Navigation API with view thunks, typed arguments, async loading and everything you need to ship complex apps, at only {size} br.
home.trace.intro: Pick a tab to watch one navigation run, from the navigate event to the rendered page.
home.trace.caption.overview: Data was ready in 72ms, inside holdCommit. The URL and the page changed together, and no loading state was shown.
home.trace.caption.members: Still loading at 300ms, so holdCommit let the URL move while the old page stayed up. Data landed before loadingDelay ran out, so no loading view flashed.
home.trace.caption.activity: Slow data. The URL moved at 300ms, the loading view took over after loadingDelay, and loadingMin kept it up for 500ms so it never flickers.
home.trace.caption.settings: A permission guard refused, and the redirect happened before commit. The URL went straight to /sign-in, so /settings never entered history.
home.trace.caption.back: A traverse back. The result was stored on the history entry, so nothing was fetched and the page came back in 14ms.
home.cohort.title: Built for 2026 without tech debt
home.cohort.baseline.title: Supported in every major browser since 2026
home.cohort.them: React Router, Next.js, TanStack, Vue Router, SvelteKit and Angular all route on the History API, pushState and popstate.
home.cohort.old.label: Built on the History API
home.cohort.next.title: Next.js builds its router into its own runtime, so it can't be measured apart
home.routes.title: Your whole app in one glance
home.routes.lede: Each route declares its path, params, data and view in one place. Data flows down from the site to the section to the page, and each page adds only what it needs.
home.routes.fact.params: Typed params and query Defaults and allowed values, checked before your code sees them.
home.routes.fact.data: Data cascades Each route's data gets what the routes above it loaded, and moving between pages reruns only the page's.
home.routes.fact.lazy: Lazy views lazy(() => import('./members.js')) splits a route out of the main bundle.
home.routes.fact.guards: Guards before the URL moves permission runs first, so a page the user can't open never shows.
home.xray.label: Show the code
home.xray.note: And still missing: loading states, back and forward reusing what loaded, titles per page, error views and scroll memory.
home.slots.title: Change the page, keep everything else
home.slots.lede: Your layout leaves slots for the breadcrumbs, a sidebar, a side panel and the page. Each route sends its pieces into the slots they belong in. When someone navigates, only the pieces that changed are replaced; the header, the nav and whatever was typed into them stay exactly as they were.
home.slots.story: A looping animation of a team app. Opening the team fills the sidebar and breadcrumbs with the team's own nav and trail. Moving between the team's pages replaces only the page area. The members page takes over the breadcrumbs and opens a side panel, and gives both back when you leave it. Leaving the team removes its pieces, and those slots show their defaults again. The header is never replaced.
home.slots.tree.label: Routes: pick one to show its page
home.try.title: Edit a running app
home.try.lede: A small nav-router app, built and served in your browser. Change a route and the preview rebuilds as you type. Nothing to install.
home.try.label: Live example: your first router
home.plugins.title: Small core, opt-in plugins
home.plugins.lede: Like day.js, the core does one job and plugins add the rest. Each one wraps a single moment in the router and calls through, so you only ship what you install.
home.plugin.head: Title, meta and canonical tags per page
home.plugin.view-transitions: Each page change inside a view transition
home.plugin.announcer: Tells screen readers the page changed

home.plugin.chunk-reload: Recovers when a deploy removes old chunks
home.plugin.timeline: Navigations in the devtools performance panel
home.plugin.sitemap: Every route, for a crawler or generator
home.adapters.title: One router, any view layer
home.adapters.lede: The core renders nothing. Each integration fills three hooks, create, update and destroy, so your routes stay the same whichever you pick.
home.adapters.plain: Plain DOM with nothing to add: strings, elements or web components.
home.adapters.react: Route views as components, with hooks for the page and its pending state.
home.adapters.preact: The React adapter’s shape at Preact’s size.
home.adapters.solid: Route data as fine-grained stores that update only what changed.
home.adapters.vue: Route views as Vue components, route data as reactive state.
home.adapters.svelte: Route views as Svelte components, route data as reactive state.
home.adapters.semantic: Route views as Templates or web components, route data as signals.

plugins.callout.title: Need something else?
plugins.callout.body: A plugin is a module you import: it wraps one moment in the router and calls through. Writing a plugin covers the moments you can wrap.
plugins.head.description: Title, meta tags and canonical link for each page, merged down the active routes.
plugins.view-transitions.description: Crosses each page change inside a view transition, so what leaves animates out and what appears animates in.
plugins.announcer.description: Announces each new page through a live region, where Safari stays silent on intercepted navigations.
plugins.confirm-leave.description: Holds unsaved forms and edits across link clicks, back and forward, and closing the tab.
plugins.preload-intent.description: Warms a link’s view code on hover, focus or touch, and adds `router.preload()` for warming one by hand.
plugins.chunk-reload.description: Recovers once when a fresh deploy has removed the old code chunk a page needs.
plugins.timeline.description: Draws each navigation and its steps in the devtools performance panel.
plugins.sitemap.description: Lists every route as a page a crawler or a generator can read, and adds `router.sitemap()`.
